boards.title: Your First Weekend at Gonzaga University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend route through Gonzaga’s named campus gathering places, from arrival landmarks to a final classroom-finding stop.

cards.title: Begin at the St. Ignatius Statue
cards.subtitle: Arrival landmark for a campus-orientation loop
cards.notes: Use the statue as a clear meetup point, then orient yourself to nearby walkways before heading toward the main campus gathering areas.
cards.short_summary: A named starting landmark for getting your bearings.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga’s 2026 Welcome Weekend schedule lists campus tours leaving from the St. Ignatius Statue.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; follow posted campus guidance for any scheduled tour.

cards.title: Meet up on Foley Lawn
cards.subtitle: Open-air gathering stop near the center of campus
cards.notes: Pause here to connect with people from your move-in group, then use the lawn as an easy visual reference for the next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A named lawn used for Welcome Weekend check-in and activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga’s 2026 Welcome Weekend schedule places new-student check-in, a block party, and evening activities on Foley Lawn.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor programming and availability vary; consult the current university schedule.

cards.title: Find the resource fair at Herak Quad
cards.subtitle: Campus quad used for orientation gatherings
cards.notes: Take a pass through the quad to identify campus resources and note the paths that connect it to academic and student-life buildings.
cards.short_summary: A named quad used for Gonzaga’s new-student resource fair.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga’s 2026 Welcome Weekend schedule lists ZagFest, a community resource fair, at Herak Quad.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; event use and access can change with the campus calendar.

cards.title: Get oriented inside Hemmingson
cards.subtitle: Campus hub for dining, meetings, and programs
cards.notes: Walk through the center and locate the welcome desk, meeting areas, and dining levels so the building is easier to use later in the weekend.
cards.short_summary: A central campus building with dining and programmed spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga identifies the John J. Hemmingson Center as offering dining options, meeting spaces, and lounge spaces.
cards.source_title: John J. Hemmingson Center | Gonzaga University
cards.access_notes: Academic-year building hours are listed as 7 a.m.–10 p.m. weekdays and 8 a.m.–9 p.m. weekends; seasonal hours differ.

cards.title: Plan a meal stop at The COG
cards.subtitle: Resident dining in the Hemmingson Center
cards.notes: Use this stop to see the dining setup and decide what fits your meal plan or budget before continuing to the evening’s campus programming.
cards.short_summary: The resident dining hall in Hemmingson Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga describes The COG as its resident dining hall, located on the first and second floors of Hemmingson Center.
cards.access_notes: Dining hours and menus are published by location and may change.

cards.title: Join an outdoor activity at Mulligan Field
cards.subtitle: Named field used for Welcome Weekend programming
cards.notes: Keep this field on your mental campus map for large outdoor gatherings, and check the current schedule before making it your evening destination.
cards.short_summary: A named field used for Playfair and class-photo programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga’s 2026 Welcome Weekend schedule lists Playfair and the Class of 2030 picture at Mulligan Field.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor programming is schedule-dependent; check current event information.

cards.title: See a major campus gathering space
cards.subtitle: Athletic center used for new-student welcome events
cards.notes: Locate the building during daylight, then check Gonzaga’s event information if you plan to return for a welcome program or athletic event.
cards.short_summary: A named athletic center that hosts Welcome Weekend gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga’s 2026 Welcome Weekend schedule lists Student Welcome Night and the President’s Welcome at McCarthey Athletic Center.
cards.access_notes: Entry requirements vary by event; verify the current event listing before attending.

cards.title: Locate St. Aloysius Church
cards.subtitle: Campus-adjacent church used for academic convocation
cards.notes: Add this landmark to your campus walk so you can find it easily if a university ceremony, service, or other scheduled program brings you here.
cards.short_summary: A named church used for Gonzaga’s academic convocation.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga’s 2026 Welcome Weekend schedule lists Academic Convocation at St. Aloysius Church.
cards.access_notes: Check the university or parish schedule before attending a service or event.

cards.title: Walk the Johnston Family Mall
cards.subtitle: Processional campus route between orientation stops
cards.notes: Use the mall as a pedestrian connector and look for wayfinding signs as you move between the quad, church, and nearby academic buildings.
cards.short_summary: A named campus mall used for Gonzaga’s welcome procession.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga’s 2026 Welcome Weekend schedule lists the Welcome Procession on Johnston Family Mall.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor route; allow for temporary closures or event setup.

cards.title: End by finding Crosby Center
cards.subtitle: Academic building used for classroom-finding support
cards.notes: Bring your fall schedule and use the nearby campus paths to practice the first walk to your classrooms before the first full week begins.
cards.short_summary: A named academic destination for classroom-finding programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga’s 2026 Welcome Weekend schedule lists a Find Your Classrooms program at the Crosby Center steps.
cards.access_notes: Classroom-finding support is schedule-dependent; use the current campus map for self-guided navigation.
